You take a normal screenshot of the game, the app sends it to the DeckMate server by itself, the server reads the opponent nick and clan, finds the deck and shows it to you: over the game screen or in Telegram.

Step 1. Get the key. Open Telegram, find the DeckMate bot and send it /scoutkey. The bot answers with a long set of letters and digits, that is your personal key. Tap it to copy.

Step 2. Paste the key. Come back here, tap the Key field in block 1 and paste (long press, Paste). Tap Save, then Check. You should see Key works.

Step 3. Turn on auto-send. In block 2 tap Allow notifications and Allow access to photos (choose Allow access to all photos), then turn on Watch for screenshots. Android shows an icon while the app works.

Step 4 (optional). Deck on screen. In block 3 turn the switch on, grant Display over other apps (settings open: turn it on and come back), tap Set position and size and drag the strip where you like.

Step 5. In the game tap Battle. When the opponent nick is visible in the top left corner, take a normal screenshot (power and volume down). In a few seconds the deck appears on the screen or in Telegram.

Yes. The app sends to the DeckMate server the screenshots you took yourself, over a secure connection. It does not read or ask for passwords, chats or data of other apps.

The key is stored on the phone encrypted and is only needed so the server knows whom to return the deck to. If the key got to the wrong place, send /scoutkey to the bot: the old key stops working at once.

The app itself does not save screenshots. Your screenshot stays in the gallery, delete it if you do not need it.

Why the permissions: Internet to send the shot. Photos to notice a new screenshot. Notifications to show that the app is working. Display over other apps only for the deck strip.

You take a normal screenshot of the battle screen. The app sends it to DeckMate by itself, finds the opponent deck and shows it: over the game or in Telegram. Setup takes two minutes.
Open Telegram, find the DeckMate bot and send it /scoutkey. The bot sends a long key: tap it to copy, come back here, paste it into the field and tap Save, then Check.
Allow notifications and access to all photos, then turn on screenshot watching. This way the app notices your screenshot and sends it.
You can show the deck as a see-through strip over the game. Turn the switch on, grant the permission and drag the strip where you like. Skip this step if you want the deck in Telegram.
Tap Check setup: the app checks the key, the server connection and the permissions and tells what to fix. Then in the game take a screenshot of the battle when the opponent nick is visible.
Extra: you can add the DeckMate tile to quick settings (pencil icon, drag the tile).
